title: Coherent completion on an open over-site with normalized projections
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $J$ ideal sheaf data, and $H$ a coherent module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For any open $W$, put $E=\operatorname{overEquiv}(W)$. The module $E(H|_{\operatorname{Over}(W)})$ is coherent. There exists an isomorphism of systems $c:E((H^\wedge)|_{\operatorname{Over}(W)})\cong (E(H|_{\operatorname{Over}(W)}))^\wedge$, with ideal $J|_W$, such that for every $n$, $E(\pi_{H,n}|_W)c_n=\pi_{E(H|_W),n}$. No affineness, nonemptiness, or covering hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), first sentence of proof: Zariski locality by uniqueness; completion functor equation 0880

proof.text: Restrict H along W.ι using coherent_module_local_on_open_cover. Transfer coherence through overFunctorEquiv: use the locally Noetherian criterion; quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism and local finite generating sections transfer along its inverse.

Apply torsionControlled_formal_restriction to the identity of the completion of H, exponent zero. Its kernel and cokernel are zero and their ideal-power products are zero by the monic product inclusions. This supplies a normalized restriction-system comparison.

Whisker overFunctorEquiv with the completion system, then compose the supplied comparison and the completion of the inverse module isomorphism. Naturality of overFunctorEquiv, the supplied projection equation, cokernel.π_desc, and cancellation of the module isomorphism prove the displayed projection normalization.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentCompletion_over_normalization
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : CoherentModules X) (W : X.Opens) :
    RingedSpace.IsCoherent W.toScheme.toRingedSpace
      ((Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W).functor.obj (H.obj.over W)) ∧
    ∃ c : (formalCompletionSystem J H.obj ⋙
        SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) W ⋙
        (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W).functor) ≅
      formalCompletionSystem (J.comap W.ι)
        ((Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W).functor.obj (H.obj.over W)),
      ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ,
        (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W).functor.map
            ((formalModuleQuotientπ J (n.unop + 1) H.obj).over W) ≫ c.hom.app n =
          formalModuleQuotientπ (J.comap W.ι) (n.unop + 1)
            ((Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W).functor.obj (H.obj.over W))
